mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 20-day window with similar FEDFUNDS path (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 5% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly higher than during periods with similar labor indicators but neutral or weak employment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which raises expected future profits and supports positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth exceeds 0.3% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the sustained consumption growth (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month coincides with a decline in inventory levels (not in the catalog but implied by context) and predicts a supply-side shock that depresses equity valuations, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly lower than during prior periods of similar INDPRO declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the federal funds rate turns positive (signaling tightening), the discount rate applied to future dividends rises, reducing the present value of expected future cash flows and generating negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not statistically lower than during prior periods of similar rate paths (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in job openings (not in the catalog but implied by context) while employment remains steady suggests a cooling labor market, lowering consumer sentiment and equity prices, resulting in negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS shows no significant change while job openings (external proxy) decline sharply (trigger condition untestable via
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly worse than during periods of stable employment and rising openings (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of industrial production below trend (INDPRO < 100) combined with rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3% month-over-month) indicate supply constraints, which typically precede equity market volatility and negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO remains below 100 for two consecutive months while CPIAUCSL increases by > 3% in the same months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly negative when similar supply indicators are absent or less pronounced (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 1% for three months), the equity risk premium tends to widen as investors discount future cash flows at lower rates, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS remains below 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not outperform a neutral benchmark (zero return) during the easing period (t-test p > 0.05).
